payout_quote: Listing your RV on RVshare is free. There are no upfront or monthly fees to create or maintain a listing. Once you receive a booking, a commission is applied and automatically deducted from your payout. The default commission rate starts at 25%.
steps: Create a free RVshare owner listing with detailed features and plenty of interior/exterior photos; vehicles must generally be 15 years old or newer for coverage eligibility.
Review incoming reservation requests and approve renters; RVshare verifies renter ID before booking.
Meet the renter for pickup with a walkthrough/demo, and record the RV's condition with photos.
On return, inspect the rig, submit any post-trip fees through the Return Form within 72 hours, and file claims against the security deposit if needed.
Receive payouts via direct deposit with the commission deducted automatically; owners can earn reduced commission rates through annual performance review.
catches: RVshare's default commission starts at 25% of the rental price and fees - a quarter of your revenue goes to the platform on every booking, reducible only through high completed-booking volume.

Earnings are fully variable: you set nightly rates but income depends on rig type, condition, location, season, and demand; figures like '$40,000/year' and 'earning potential of $38,000 a year' (Class C) are marketing illustrations, not guarantees.

RVshare's own blog marketing has claimed 'no commission' in places (its 2024 consignment blog post says 'there is no commission'), which directly contradicts the official help center's 25% default commission - rely on your account's displayed rate, not marketing copy.

Insurance is not blanket coverage: RVshare Rental Insurance provides $1M liability plus comprehensive/collision up to $200,000, but only for rigs 15 years old or newer; older vehicles cannot be listed.
RVs are high-wear assets: deep cleaning every turnover, tire/brake inspections, maintenance (~20% of revenue rule of thumb), damage risk, and loan terms that may prohibit commercial rental.
Rental income is taxable; you are responsible for taxes, and some owners list tax separately on listings.
Cancellation policies are owner-chosen (Flexible/Standard/Strict) - owner cancellations are excluded from commission-rate review and repeated cancellations hurt performance.
biggest_catch: RVshare keeps a default 25% commission on every booking and income is entirely demand-driven, so you keep at most 75% of a self-set rate minus cleaning, maintenance, and wear costs - and RVshare's own marketing has contradictorily claimed 'no commission' on its blog, so trust only the rate shown in your account.
eligibility: Own a motorhome or travel trailer (15 years old or newer for platform insurance coverage); vehicles must pass listing review; comply with state registration/insurance laws and check loan terms for commercial-rental restrictions. Renters must pass ID verification.
timing: Listing is free and self-serve; commission deducted automatically at booking. Payouts go to your bank account via direct deposit; first booking depends on rig, market, and season and can take weeks or months.
